literal: Possessing good conduct is noble birth; misconduct will end up becoming a lowly birth.
translation: Possessing good conduct constitutes true noble birth; slipping into misconduct will result in being reduced to a lowly birth.
modern: ஒழுக்கத்தைக் கொண்டிருப்பதே நற்குடிப் பிறப்பாகும்; ஒழுக்கத்திலிருந்து தவறுதல் இழிவான பிறப்பாக முடிந்துவிடும்.
explanation: This couplet redefines nobility and lowliness based on personal character rather than ancestry. Having good conduct (oḻukkam utaimai) is what truly constitutes a noble lineage (kutimai). Conversely, slipping from moral standards (iḻukkam) degrades a person, making them equivalent to one of lowly birth (iḻinta piṟappu), regardless of their actual family background. The poet emphasizes that true status is earned through behavior, not inherited.
